title: A Human Appeared Behind the Scenes of AI Phone Calls
part1:
Meta’s personal AI agent, Muse, is a service that can call businesses and stores to make a haircut appointment, check whether something is in stock, or get a price quote from a service provider. But in some of these calls, the cast unexpectedly changed.

The callers were not AI, but trained human contract workers. They were responsible not only for making the calls, but also for completing the conversation with the other person to the end.

This test was called “human concierges” or “human agent calls.” Behind a service in which AI makes phone calls, humans were making the calls. Even its name suggests a slightly strange setup.
part2:
Then the phone drama became even more complicated. Reports based on internal posts described cases in which people hung up when they realized Muse was AI. One employee reported that an insurance company repeatedly hung up whenever it learned that the call from Muse had been made by AI.

On the other hand, human-handled calls raised another problem. Meta employees voiced concern that sensitive information needed to move the call forward might be shared unintentionally with contract workers at a call center. In addition, in one case where Meta asked someone to negotiate internet and cable fees, a report said that the call record contained inappropriate remarks about race.

A Meta spokesperson explained that the employees’ reaction had been “overwhelmingly positive.” The spokesperson said it was a test to put safety and privacy protections in place and make improvements before the service was released to the public.
part3:
However, a vice president in Meta’s Superintelligence Labs division admitted in an internal post that starting the test with contract workers making the calls, without proper disclosure, had been a “mistake.” The human concierge feature will be rolled back for now. Meta did not stop Muse as a whole; it only rolled back this feature for the time being.

The moment humans entered AI’s phone calls, the people on the other end, the handling of information, and the way it was explained all took center stage. The key point this time was not that AI spoke like a human. It was how to tell people that a human had appeared.
in_one_line: Meta temporarily rolled back a phone-calling feature after it emerged that humans, not AI, handled some calls.
